title.zh: 卷二十三 志第三: 禮儀三
title.raw: 卷二十三 志第三: 禮儀三 Volume 23 Treatises 3: Rites 3

sentences.zh: 封禪之禮，自漢光武之後，曠世不修。

translations.literal: The rites of feng and shan, after Emperor Guangwu of Han, went unrepaired for generations.
translations.idiomatic: After Han Guangwu, the feng and shan rites went unrepaired for generations.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇十四年，晉王廣率百官抗表，固請封禪。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Sui Kaihuang, Prince of Jin Yang Guang led the hundred officials in submitting a memorial firmly requesting feng and shan.
translations.idiomatic: In Sui Kaihuang 14, Prince of Jin Yang Guang led officials in a memorial firmly requesting feng and shan.

sentences.zh: 文帝令牛弘、辛彥之、許善心等創定儀注。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen ordered Niu Hong, Xin Yanzhi, Xu Shansin, and others to draft ritual regulations anew.
translations.idiomatic: Wendi ordered Niu Hong, Xin Yanzhi, Xu Shansin, and others to draft new ritual regulations.

sentences.zh: 至十五年，行幸兗州，遂於太山之下，為壇設祭，如南郊之禮，竟不升山而還。

translations.literal: By the fifteenth year, on a progress to Yanzhou, he set up an altar and offered sacrifice below Mount Tai, as in the southern suburban rite, but in the end did not ascend the mountain and returned.
translations.idiomatic: By year 15, touring Yanzhou, he set an altar below Mount Tai and sacrificed as at the southern suburb—but never ascended and returned.

sentences.zh: 貞觀六年，平突厥，年穀屢登，群臣上言請封泰山。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhenguan, after pacifying the Turks and repeated good harvests, the ministers memorialized requesting feng at Mount Tai.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 6, with the Turks pacified and harvests full, ministers asked to feng Mount Tai.

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「議者以封禪為大典。

translations.literal: Taizong said: "Those who debate take feng and shan as a great ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said, "Debaters call feng and shan a grand ceremony.

sentences.zh: 如朕本心，但使天下太平，家給人足，雖闕封禪之禮，亦可比德堯、舜；

translations.literal: As for my own heart, if only the realm is at peace and every household has enough, even lacking the rites of feng and shan, one may still match the virtue of Yao and Shun;
translations.idiomatic: In my heart, if the realm is peaceful and households prosper, even without feng and shan one may match Yao and Shun;

sentences.zh: 若百姓不足，夷狄內侵，縱修封禪之儀，亦何異於桀、紂？

translations.literal: if the people are not sufficient and barbarians invade within, even if one performs the ceremonies of feng and shan, how is it different from Jie and Zhou?
translations.idiomatic: if the people lack and barbarians invade, feng and shan ceremonies would differ little from Jie and Zhou.

sentences.zh: 昔秦始皇自謂德洽天心，自稱皇帝，登封岱宗，奢侈自矜。

translations.literal: In former times Qin Shihuang considered his virtue in accord with Heaven's heart, styled himself emperor, ascended to feng at Dai, and was extravagant and self-congratulatory.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Shihuang deemed his virtue Heaven's will, called himself emperor, fenged at Dai, and luxuriated in pride.

sentences.zh: 漢文帝竟不登封，而躬行儉約，刑措不用。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Han in the end did not ascend to feng, yet personally practiced frugality, and punishments went unused.
translations.idiomatic: Han Wendi never fenged, yet practiced frugality and left punishments unused.

sentences.zh: 今皆稱始皇為暴虐之主，漢文為有德之君。

translations.literal: Now all call the First Emperor a tyrannical ruler and Emperor Wen of Han a ruler of virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Today the First Emperor is called tyrannical and Wendi virtuous.

sentences.zh: 以此而言，無假封禪。

translations.literal: Judging by this, there is no need for feng and shan.
translations.idiomatic: By this measure, feng and shan are unnecessary.

sentences.zh: 禮雲，'至敬不壇'，掃地而祭，足表至誠，何必遠登高山，封數尺之土也！」

translations.literal: The Rites say, 'supreme reverence needs no altar'—sweeping the ground to sacrifice suffices to show utmost sincerity; why must one climb far mountains and enclose a few feet of earth!"
translations.idiomatic: The Rites say, 'supreme reverence needs no altar'—sweeping ground to sacrifice shows utmost sincerity; why climb mountains to seal a few feet of earth?"

sentences.zh: 侍中王珪對曰：「陛下發德音，明封禪本末，非愚臣之所及。」

translations.literal: Attendant-in-ordinary Wang Gui replied: "Your Majesty has issued virtuous words clarifying the roots and branches of feng and shan—beyond what this foolish minister can reach."
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Wang Gui replied, "Your Majesty's virtuous words clarify feng and shan's roots and branches—beyond this fool's reach."

sentences.zh: 秘書監魏征曰：「隨末大亂，黎民遇陛下，始有生望。

translations.literal: Secretariat Director Wei Zheng said: "After the chaos at the end of Sui, the people met Your Majesty and first had hope of life.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Director Wei Zheng said, "After late-Sui chaos, the people met you and first hoped to live.

sentences.zh: 養之則至仁，勞之則未可。

translations.literal: To nourish them is utmost benevolence; to labor them is not yet permissible.
translations.idiomatic: Nourishing them is utmost benevolence; laboring them is not yet fit.

sentences.zh: 升中之禮，須備千乘萬騎，供帳之費，動役數州。

translations.literal: The ceremony of ascending and libation requires thousands of chariots and ten thousands of riders; the cost of supplies and pavilions would mobilize several provinces.
translations.idiomatic: The ascent-and-libation rite needs thousands of chariots and myriad riders; supply costs would mobilize several provinces.

sentences.zh: 戶口蕭條，何以能給？」

translations.literal: Households are desolate—how could it be supplied?"
translations.idiomatic: Households are desolate—how could it be supplied?"

sentences.zh: 太宗深嘉征言，而中外章表不已。

translations.literal: Taizong deeply praised Zheng's words, but memorials from within and without did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong deeply praised Zheng, yet memorials inside and out did not cease.

sentences.zh: 上問禮官兩漢封山儀注，因遣中書侍郎杜正倫行太山上七十二帝壇跡。

translations.literal: The emperor asked the ritual officials about the ceremonies of fenging mountains in the two Han dynasties, and dispatched Secretariat Vice Director Du Zhenlun to trace the altar sites of the seventy-two emperors on Mount Tai.
translations.idiomatic: He asked ritual officials about Han feng ceremonies and sent Du Zhenlun to trace the seventy-two emperors' altars on Mount Tai.

sentences.zh: 是年兩河水潦，其事乃寢。

translations.literal: That year both rivers flooded, and the affair was laid to rest.
translations.idiomatic: That year both rivers flooded, and the matter rested.

sentences.zh: 至十一年，群臣復勸封山，始議其禮。

translations.literal: By the eleventh year, the ministers again urged fenging the mountain, and discussion of the rites began.
translations.idiomatic: By year 11 ministers again urged fenging, and rite discussions began.

sentences.zh: 於是國子博士劉伯莊、睦州刺史徐令言等，各上封祀之事，互設疑議，所見不同。

translations.literal: Thereupon National University Erudite Liu Bozhuang, Muzhou Prefect Xu Lingyan, and others each submitted proposals on feng and sacrifice, setting forth doubts and disputes; their views differed.
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Liu Bozhuang, Prefect Xu Lingyan, and others submitted feng proposals with conflicting doubts.

sentences.zh: 多言新禮中封禪儀注，簡略未周。

translations.literal: Many said the feng and shan regulations in the new rites were brief and not complete.
translations.idiomatic: Many said new-rite feng and shan regulations were brief and incomplete.

sentences.zh: 太宗敕秘書少監顏思古、諫議大夫硃子奢等，與四方名儒博物之士參議得失。

translations.literal: Taizong ordered Secretariat Vice Director Yan Sigu, Remonstrance and Correction Grandee Zhu Zishe, and others, together with renowned Confucians and men of broad learning from all quarters, to deliberate gains and losses.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong ordered Yan Sigu, Zhu Zishe, and renowned scholars from all quarters to debate gains and losses.

sentences.zh: 議者數十家，遞相駁難，紛紜久不決。

translations.literal: Several tens of schools debated, each refuting the other; confusion long went unresolved.
translations.idiomatic: Dozens of schools refuted one another; confusion long went unresolved.

sentences.zh: 於是左僕射房玄齡、特進魏征、中書令楊師道，博采眾議堪行用而與舊禮不同者奏之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Fang Xuanling, Special Grandee Wei Zheng, and Central Secretariat Director Yang Shidao broadly gathered proposals fit for use that differed from old rites and submitted them.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xuanling, Wei Zheng, and Yang Shidao gathered workable proposals differing from old rites and submitted them.

sentences.zh: 其議昊天上帝壇曰：「將封先祭，義在告神，且備謁敬之儀，方展慶成之禮。

translations.literal: Their proposal on the altar to August Heaven said: "Before feng one first sacrifices—the meaning is to announce to the spirits; moreover one prepares the rites of audience and reverence, then unfolds the rite of celebrating completion.
translations.idiomatic: On the August Heaven altar: "Before feng, sacrifice first—to announce to spirits and prepare audience rites before celebrating completion.

sentences.zh: 固當於壇下阯，預申齊潔。

translations.literal: Surely one should beforehand at the foot of the altar perform purification.
translations.idiomatic: Surely purification should precede at the altar foot.

sentences.zh: 贊饗已畢，然後登封。

translations.literal: When the assisting sacrifice is finished, then ascend to feng.
translations.idiomatic: When assisting sacrifice ends, then ascend to feng.

sentences.zh: 既表重慎之深，兼示行事有漸。

translations.literal: This both shows the depth of weighty caution and displays that the undertaking proceeds by stages.
translations.idiomatic: This shows deep caution and staged procedure.

sentences.zh: 今請祭于泰山下，設壇以祀上帝，以景皇帝配享。

translations.literal: Now we request sacrifice below Mount Tai, setting an altar to worship August Heaven, with Emperor Jing as associate offering.
translations.idiomatic: We request sacrifice below Mount Tai, worshipping August Heaven with Emperor Jing as associate.

sentences.zh: 壇長一十二丈，高一丈二尺。」

translations.literal: The altar is twelve zhang long and one zhang two chi high."
translations.idiomatic: The altar is twelve zhang long and one zhang two chi high."

sentences.zh: 又議制玉牒曰：「金玉重寶，質性貞堅，宗祀郊禋，皆充器幣，豈嫌華美，實貴精確。

translations.literal: They also proposed on making the jade tablet: "Gold and jade are heavy treasures; their substance is firm and true; in ancestral and suburban sacrifices they all serve as vessels and offerings—who would disdain their splendor? What is valued is precision.
translations.idiomatic: On the jade tablet: "Gold and jade are heavy treasures, firm and true; in ancestral and suburban rites they serve as vessels—splendor is not disdained; precision is valued.

sentences.zh: 況乎三神壯觀，萬代鴻名，禮極殷崇，事資藻縟。

translations.literal: How much more for the magnificent sight of the three spirits and a great name for ten thousand generations—the rites reach utmost honor and the affair requires full ornament.
translations.idiomatic: For the three spirits' magnificent sight and a name for ten thousand generations, rites reach utmost honor and require full ornament.

sentences.zh: 玉牒玉檢，式韞靈奇，

translations.literal: Jade tablet and jade clasp enfold spiritual wonder,
translations.idiomatic: Jade tablet and jade clasp enfold spiritual wonder,

sentences.zh: 傳之無窮，永存不朽。

translations.literal: transmitted without end, stored forever without decay.
translations.idiomatic: transmitted without end, stored forever without decay.

sentences.zh: 今請玉牒長一尺三寸，廣厚各五寸。

translations.literal: Now we request the jade tablet one chi three cun long, five cun wide and thick each.
translations.idiomatic: We request the jade tablet one chi three cun long, five cun wide and thick.

sentences.zh: 玉檢厚二寸，長短闊狹一如玉牒。

translations.literal: The jade clasp two cun thick, length, width, and breadth the same as the jade tablet.
translations.idiomatic: The jade clasp two cun thick, dimensions matching the tablet.

sentences.zh: 其印齒請隨璽大小，仍纏以金繩五周。」

translations.literal: For the seal teeth, follow the size of the seal; still wrap with gold cord five circuits."
translations.idiomatic: Seal teeth follow seal size; wrap with gold cord five circuits."

sentences.zh: 又議玉策曰：「封禪之祭，嚴配作主，皆奠玉策，肅奉虔誠。

translations.literal: They also proposed on jade slips: "In the feng and shan sacrifice, solemn matching makes the chief offering; all set down jade slips, reverently offering sincere devotion.
translations.idiomatic: On jade slips: "In feng and shan, solemn matching makes the chief offering; all set jade slips in reverent devotion.

sentences.zh: 今玉策四枚，各長一尺三寸，廣一寸五分，厚五分。

translations.literal: Now four jade slips, each one chi three cun long, one cun five fen wide, five fen thick.
translations.idiomatic: Now four jade slips, each one chi three cun long, one cun five fen wide, five fen thick.

sentences.zh: 每策五簡，俱以金編。

translations.literal: Each slip has five tablets, all bound with gold.
translations.idiomatic: Each slip has five tablets, all gold-bound.

sentences.zh: 其一奠上帝，一奠太祖座，一奠皇地祇，一奠高祖座。」

translations.literal: One is set for August Heaven, one for the seat of the Great Ancestor, one for Imperial Earth Sovereign, one for the seat of the High Ancestor."
translations.idiomatic: One for August Heaven, one for the Great Ancestor's seat, one for Imperial Earth Sovereign, one for the High Ancestor's seat."

sentences.zh: 又議金匱曰：「登配之策，盛以金匱，歸格藝祖之廟室。

translations.literal: They also proposed on the gold casket: "Slips for ascent and matching are stored in a gold casket and returned to the temple chamber of the Artistic Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: On the gold casket: "Ascent-and-matching slips go in a gold casket returned to the Artistic Ancestor's temple.

sentences.zh: 今請長短令容玉策，高廣各六寸。

translations.literal: Now we request length and breadth to hold the jade slips, height and width six cun each.
translations.idiomatic: We request dimensions to hold the slips, six cun high and wide.

sentences.zh: 形制如今之表函。

translations.literal: The form like present memorial cases.
translations.idiomatic: Form like present memorial cases.

sentences.zh: 纏以金繩，封以金泥，印以受命璽。」

translations.literal: Wrap with gold cord, seal with gold mud, impress with the Seal of Receiving the Mandate."
translations.idiomatic: Wrap with gold cord, seal with gold mud, impress with the Seal of Receiving the Mandate."

sentences.zh: 又議方石再累曰：「舊藏玉牒，止用石函，亦猶盛書篋笥，所以或呼石篋。

translations.literal: They also proposed on square stones in layers: "Formerly in storing the jade tablet only a stone case was used—like storing books in cases; hence it was sometimes called a stone case.
translations.idiomatic: On layered square stones: "Formerly the jade tablet was stored in a stone case, like a book case—sometimes called a stone case.

sentences.zh: 今請方石三枚，以為再累。

translations.literal: Now we request three square stones as further layers.
translations.idiomatic: We request three square stones as further layers.

sentences.zh: 其十枚石檢，刻方石四邊而立之。

translations.literal: Ten stone clasps are carved on the four sides of the square stone and set upright.
translations.idiomatic: Ten stone clasps are carved on the square stone's four sides and set upright.

sentences.zh: 纏以金繩，封以石泥，印以受命璽。」

translations.literal: Wrap with gold cord, seal with stone mud, impress with the Seal of Receiving the Mandate."
translations.idiomatic: Wrap with gold cord, seal with stone mud, impress with the Seal of Receiving the Mandate."

sentences.zh: 又議泰山上圓壇曰：「四出開道，壇場通義，南面入升，於事為允。

translations.literal: They also proposed on the round altar atop Mount Tai: "Opening roads on four sides and an altar field is the common meaning; entering and ascending from the south is fitting in the affair.
translations.idiomatic: On Tai's round altar: "Four roads open from the altar field; ascending from the south is fitting.

sentences.zh: 今請介丘上圓壇廣五丈，高九尺，用五色土加之。

translations.literal: Now we request on the round altar atop Jie Hill a width of five zhang and height nine chi, with five-colored earth added.
translations.idiomatic: We request Jie Hill's round altar five zhang wide, nine chi high, with five-colored earth.

sentences.zh: 四面各設一階。

translations.literal: On each of the four sides set one flight of steps.
translations.idiomatic: Each side has one flight of steps.

sentences.zh: 御位在壇南，升自南階，而就上封玉牒。」

translations.literal: The imperial position is south of the altar; ascend from the southern steps and perform feng with the jade tablet upon it."
translations.idiomatic: The imperial position is south of the altar; ascend the southern steps to feng with the jade tablet."

sentences.zh: 又議圓壇上土封曰：「凡言封者，皆是積土之名。

translations.literal: They also proposed on earthen sealing atop the round altar: "Whenever one speaks of feng, it is always the name of heaping earth.
translations.idiomatic: On earthen sealing atop the round altar: "Feng always means heaping earth.

sentences.zh: 利建分封，亦以班社立號。

translations.literal: In establishing merit and dividing fiefs, one also distributes altars and establishes titles.
translations.idiomatic: Establishing merit and dividing fiefs also distributes altars and titles.

sentences.zh: 謂之封禪，厥義可知。

translations.literal: Calling it feng and shan—the meaning can be known.
translations.idiomatic: Calling it feng and shan—the meaning is clear.

sentences.zh: 今請於圓壇之上，安置方石，璽緘既畢，加土築以為封。

translations.literal: Now we request on top of the round altar to place the square stone; when sealing with the seal is finished, add earth and build it as the feng.
translations.idiomatic: We request placing the square stone atop the round altar; when sealing is done, heap earth as feng.

sentences.zh: 高一丈二尺，而廣二丈，以五色土益封，玉牒藏於其內。

translations.literal: One zhang two chi high and two zhang wide, augment the feng with five-colored earth; the jade tablet is stored within.
translations.idiomatic: One zhang two chi high, two zhang wide; augment with five-colored earth; the jade tablet is stored within.

sentences.zh: 祀禪之土，其封制亦同此。」

translations.literal: For the earth of the shan sacrifice, the form of the feng is also the same."
translations.idiomatic: For shan-sacrifice earth, the feng form is the same."

sentences.zh: 又議玉璽曰：「謹詳前載方石緘封，玉檢金泥，必資印璽，以為秘固。

translations.literal: They also proposed on the jade seal: "Carefully examining former records, square-stone sealing, jade clasp and gold mud necessarily rely on impressing seals for secret security.
translations.idiomatic: On the jade seal: "Former records show square-stone sealing and gold mud require seals for security.

sentences.zh: 今請依令用受命璽以封石檢。

translations.literal: Now we request following the ordinance to use the Seal of Receiving the Mandate to seal the stone clasps.
translations.idiomatic: We request the Seal of Receiving the Mandate to seal stone clasps.

sentences.zh: 其玉檢既與石檢大小不同，請更造璽一枚，方一寸二分，文同受命璽，以封玉牒。

translations.literal: Since the jade clasp differs in size from the stone clasp, we request another seal made, one cun two fen square, text the same as the Seal of Receiving the Mandate, to seal the jade tablet.
translations.idiomatic: Since jade and stone clasps differ in size, we request another seal, one cun two fen square, same text as the Mandate seal, for the jade tablet.

sentences.zh: 石檢形制，依漢建武故事。」

translations.literal: The form of the stone clasps follows the story of Jianwu in Han."
translations.idiomatic: Stone clasp form follows Han Jianwu precedent."

sentences.zh: 又議立碑曰：「勒石紀號，顯揚功業，登封降禪，肆覲之壇，立碑紀之。」

translations.literal: They also proposed on erecting a stele: "Carving stone to record titles and displaying achievements—in feng, descent, and libation, and altars of grand audience, erect steles to record them."
translations.idiomatic: On erecting a stele: "Carve stone to record titles and display achievements at feng, descent, libation, and grand-audience altars."

sentences.zh: 又議設告至壇曰：「既至山下，禮行告至，柴於東方上帝，望秩遍禮群神。

translations.literal: They also proposed on setting an Announce-Arrival altar: "Having reached below the mountain, perform the rite of announcing arrival; offer firewood to the Eastern Lord on High and perform ranked audience to all spirits in order.
translations.idiomatic: On the Announce-Arrival altar: "At the mountain foot, perform announcing arrival; offer firewood to the Eastern Lord on High and ranked audience to all spirits.

sentences.zh: 今請其壇方八十一尺，高三尺，陛仍四出。

translations.literal: Now we request the altar eighty-one chi square and three chi high, with steps still opening on four sides.
translations.idiomatic: We request the altar eighty-one chi square, three chi high, steps on four sides.

sentences.zh: 其禪方壇及餘儀式，請從今禮。

translations.literal: For the square altar of shan and remaining forms, we request following the present rites.
translations.idiomatic: For the shan square altar and remaining forms, follow present rites.

sentences.zh: 仍請柴祭、望秩，同時行事。」

translations.literal: Still request firewood offering and ranked audience performed at the same time."
translations.idiomatic: Request firewood offering and ranked audience at the same time."

sentences.zh: 又議廢石闕及大小距石曰：「距石之設，意取牢固，本資實用，豈雲雕飾。

translations.literal: They also proposed abolishing stone que and large and small distance-stones: "Setting distance-stones takes solidity as its meaning; originally it relies on practical use—how could it be called ornament?
translations.idiomatic: On abolishing stone que and distance-stones: "Distance-stones mean solidity and practical use—not ornament.

sentences.zh: 今既積土厚封，足與天長地久。

translations.literal: Now that heaped earth seals thickly, it suffices to match heaven in enduring long.
translations.idiomatic: Thick heaped-earth sealing suffices to endure with heaven.

sentences.zh: 其小距環壇，石闕回建，事非經誥，無益禮義，煩而非要，請從減省。」

translations.literal: Small distance-stones encircling the altar and stone que built around—such matters are not in the classics, benefit ritual meaning not at all, troublesome and not essential; we request reduction."
translations.idiomatic: Small distance-stones and encircling stone que are uncanonical, benefit ritual not at all, troublesome and inessential—reduce them."

sentences.zh: 太宗從其議，仍令附之於禮。

translations.literal: Taizong followed their proposal and still ordered it attached to the rites.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong followed their proposal and ordered it attached to the rites.

sentences.zh: 十五年，下詔，將有事于泰山，復令公卿諸儒詳定儀注。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year an edict was issued: there would be affairs at Mount Tai; again he ordered dukes, ministers, and Confucians to fix the ritual regulations in detail.
translations.idiomatic: In year 15 an edict announced affairs at Mount Tai and ordered dukes, ministers, and Confucians to fix regulations.

sentences.zh: 太常卿韋挺、禮部侍郎令狐德棻為封禪使，參考其議。

translations.literal: Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Wei Ting and Vice Minister of Rites Linghu Defen served as feng and shan commissioners and consulted their proposals.
translations.idiomatic: Court of Sacrifices Director Wei Ting and Rites Vice Minister Linghu Defen served as feng-shan commissioners.

sentences.zh: 時論者又執異見，顏師古上書申明前議。

translations.literal: At the time debaters again held differing views; Yan Shigu submitted a memorial clarifying the former proposals.
translations.idiomatic: Debaters again differed; Yan Shigu submitted a memorial clarifying earlier proposals.

sentences.zh: 太宗覽其奏，多依師古所陳為定。

translations.literal: Taizong reviewed the memorial and largely fixed matters according to what Shigu stated.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong reviewed it and largely fixed matters per Shigu.

sentences.zh: 車駕至洛陽宮，會有彗星之變，乃下詔罷其事。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage reached Luoyang Palace; a comet appeared, and an edict halted the affair.
translations.idiomatic: At Luoyang Palace a comet appeared; an edict halted the affair.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，公卿數請封禪，則天既立為皇后，又密贊之。

translations.literal: After Gaozong took the throne, dukes and ministers repeatedly requested feng and shan; Wu Zetian, having been established as empress, also secretly endorsed it.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozong's accession, officials repeatedly requested feng and shan; Empress Wu secretly endorsed it.

sentences.zh: 麟德二年二月，車駕發京，東巡狩，詔禮官、博士撰定封禪儀注：

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year of Qide, the imperial carriage departed the capital on an eastern tour; he ordered ritual officials and erudites to draft feng and shan regulations:
translations.idiomatic: Qide 2, month 2, the carriage departed on an eastern tour; ritual officials and erudites were ordered to draft feng-shan regulations:

sentences.zh: 有司于乾封元年正月戊辰朔。

translations.literal: The relevant offices on the first day of the first month of the first year of Qianfeng.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices on Qianfeng 1, month 1, day 1.

sentences.zh: 先是，有司齋戒。

translations.literal: Earlier, the relevant offices had performed abstention.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the relevant offices had abstained.

sentences.zh: 于前祀七日平旦，太尉誓百官于行從中台，云：「來月一日封祀，二日登封泰山，三日禪社首，各揚其職，不供其事，國有常刑。」

translations.literal: Seven days before the prior sacrifice, at dawn, the Grand Marshal swore in the hundred officials in the traveling central terrace, saying: "On the first of next month feng and sacrifice; on the second ascend and feng Mount Tai; on the third shan at Sheshou—each perform your duty; failure brings statutory punishment."
translations.idiomatic: Seven days before sacrifice, at dawn the Grand Marshal swore in officials at the traveling terrace: "Month 1 day 1: feng sacrifice; day 2: ascend and feng Tai; day 3: shan at Sheshou—each perform your duty or face statutory punishment."

sentences.zh: 上齋於行宮四日，致齋三日。

translations.literal: The emperor abstained at the traveling palace four days and performed full abstention three days.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor abstained four days at the traveling palace and three days in full abstention.

sentences.zh: 近侍之官應從升者，及從事群官、諸方客使，各本司公館清齋一宿。

translations.literal: Close attendants who should ascend, attending officials, and envoys from all quarters each abstained one night at their offices' guest houses.
translations.idiomatic: Close attendants, attending officials, and envoys each abstained one night at their offices.

sentences.zh: 前祀一日，諸衛令共屬：未後一刻，設黃麾半仗於外壝之外，與樂工人俱清齋一宿。

translations.literal: One day before the prior sacrifice, the commandants of the guards jointly ordered: after the first quarter of wei, set half the yellow awning guard outside the outer enclosure, and musicians likewise abstained one night.
translations.idiomatic: One day before sacrifice, guard commandants ordered half the yellow awning guard outside the outer enclosure after wei quarter 1; musicians abstained one night.

sentences.zh: 有司于太岳南四里為圓壇，三成、十二階，如圓丘之制。

translations.literal: The relevant offices made a round altar four li south of Great Peak, three tiers and twelve steps, like the round mound form.
translations.idiomatic: Offices made a round altar four li south of Great Peak, three tiers and twelve steps, like the round mound.

sentences.zh: 壇上飾以青，四面各依方色，並造燎壇及壝三重。

translations.literal: The altar top was adorned with green; each of the four sides followed its directional color, and a firewood altar and triple enclosure were also made.
translations.idiomatic: The altar top was green; each side followed its color; a firewood altar and triple enclosure were made.

sentences.zh: 又造玉策三枚，皆以金繩連編玉簡為之。

translations.literal: Three jade slips were also made, all linked by gold cord binding jade tablets.
translations.idiomatic: Three jade slips were made, jade tablets linked by gold cord.

sentences.zh: 每簡長一尺二寸，廣一寸二分，厚三分，刻玉填金為字。

translations.literal: Each tablet one chi two cun long, one cun two fen wide, three fen thick, characters carved in jade and filled with gold.
translations.idiomatic: Each tablet one chi two cun long, one cun two fen wide, three fen thick, jade carved and gold-filled.

sentences.zh: 又為玉匱一，以藏正座玉策，長一尺三寸。

translations.literal: One jade casket was also made to store the chief-seat jade slip, one chi three cun long.
translations.idiomatic: One jade casket stored the chief-seat slip, one chi three cun long.

sentences.zh: 並玉檢方五寸，當繩處刻為五道，當封璽處刻深二分，方一寸二分。

translations.literal: Jade clasps five cun square; where the cord lay, five channels were carved; where the seal lay, two fen deep, one cun two fen square.
translations.idiomatic: Jade clasps five cun square; five cord channels carved; seal recess two fen deep, one cun two fen square.

sentences.zh: 又為金匱二，以藏配座玉策，制度如玉匱。

translations.literal: Two gold caskets were also made to store matching-seat jade slips, regulations like the jade casket.
translations.idiomatic: Two gold caskets stored matching-seat slips, like the jade casket.

sentences.zh: 又為黃金繩以纏金玉匱，各五周。

translations.literal: Gold cord was also made to wrap the jade and gold caskets, five circuits each.
translations.idiomatic: Gold cord wrapped jade and gold caskets, five circuits each.

sentences.zh: 為金泥、玉匱、金匱。

translations.literal: Gold mud, jade caskets, and gold caskets were made.
translations.idiomatic: Gold mud, jade caskets, and gold caskets were made.

sentences.zh: 為玉璽一枚，方一寸二分，文同受命璽，封玉匱、金匱。

translations.literal: One jade seal was made, one cun two fen square, text the same as the Seal of Receiving the Mandate, to seal jade and gold caskets.
translations.idiomatic: One jade seal, one cun two fen square, Mandate-seal text, sealed jade and gold caskets.

sentences.zh: 又為石感，以藏玉匱。

translations.literal: A stone receptacle was also made to store the jade casket.
translations.idiomatic: A stone receptacle stored the jade casket.

sentences.zh: 用方石再累，各方五尺，厚一尺，刻方石中令容玉匱。

translations.literal: Using layered square stones, each five chi square and one chi thick, the square stone was carved within to hold the jade casket.
translations.idiomatic: Layered square stones, each five chi square, one chi thick, carved within to hold the jade casket.

sentences.zh: 感旁施檢處，皆刻深三寸三分，闊一尺。

translations.literal: At the places for clasps beside the receptacle, all were carved three cun three fen deep and one chi wide.
translations.idiomatic: Clasp sites beside the receptacle were carved three cun three fen deep, one chi wide.

sentences.zh: 當繩處皆刻深三分，闊一寸五分。

translations.literal: Where cords passed, all were carved three fen deep and one cun five fen wide.
translations.idiomatic: Cord sites were carved three fen deep, one cun five fen wide.

sentences.zh: 為石檢十枚，以檢石感，皆長三尺，闊一尺，厚七寸。

translations.literal: Ten stone clasps were made to clasp the stone receptacle, all three chi long, one chi wide, seven cun thick.
translations.idiomatic: Ten stone clasps clasped the receptacle, three chi long, one chi wide, seven cun thick.

sentences.zh: 皆刻為印齒三道，深四寸。

translations.literal: All were carved with three seal teeth, four cun deep.
translations.idiomatic: All had three seal teeth carved four cun deep.

sentences.zh: 當封璽處方五寸，當通繩處闊一寸五分。

translations.literal: Where the seal lay was five cun square; where the cord passed was one cun five fen wide.
translations.idiomatic: Seal sites were five cun square; cord sites one cun five fen wide.

sentences.zh: 皆有小石蓋，制與檢刻處相應，以檢擫封泥。

translations.literal: All had small stone lids matching the clasp carvings to press sealing mud.
translations.idiomatic: All had small stone lids matching clasp carvings to press sealing mud.

sentences.zh: 其檢立於感旁，南方、北方各三，東方、西方各二，去感隅皆七寸。

translations.literal: The clasps stood beside the receptacle—three south and north, two east and west, seven cun from each corner of the receptacle.
translations.idiomatic: Clasps stood beside the receptacle—three south and north, two east and west, seven cun from corners.

sentences.zh: 又為金繩以纏石感，各五周，徑三分。

translations.literal: Gold cord was also made to wrap the stone receptacle, five circuits each, three fen in diameter.
translations.idiomatic: Gold cord wrapped the stone receptacle five circuits each, three fen diameter.

sentences.zh: 為石泥以泥石感，其泥，末石和方色土為之。

translations.literal: Stone mud sealed the stone receptacle; the mud was made of powdered stone mixed with directional-colored earth.
translations.idiomatic: Stone mud sealed the receptacle—powdered stone mixed with directional-colored earth.

sentences.zh: 為距石十二枚，分距感隅，皆再累，各闊二尺，長一丈，斜刻其首，令與感隅相應。

translations.literal: Twelve distance-stones were made, spaced at receptacle corners, all layered, each two chi wide and one zhang long, heads cut slanting to match receptacle corners.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve distance-stones at receptacle corners, layered, two chi wide, one zhang long, slanted heads matching corners.

sentences.zh: 泰山之上，設登封之壇，上徑五丈，高九尺，四出陛。

translations.literal: Atop Mount Tai an ascent-feng altar was set, five zhang top diameter, nine chi high, steps on four sides.
translations.idiomatic: Atop Mount Tai an ascent-feng altar was set, five zhang diameter, nine chi high, four flights of steps.

sentences.zh: 壇上飾以青，四面依方色。

translations.literal: The altar top was adorned with green; the four sides followed directional colors.
translations.idiomatic: The altar top was green; sides followed directional colors.

sentences.zh: 一壝，隨地之宜。

translations.literal: One enclosure, according to the terrain.
translations.idiomatic: One enclosure, according to terrain.

sentences.zh: 其玉牒、玉匱、石感、石檢、距石，皆如封祀之制。

translations.literal: The jade tablet, jade casket, stone receptacle, stone clasps, and distance-stones all followed the feng-sacrifice form.
translations.idiomatic: Jade tablet, jade casket, stone receptacle, stone clasps, and distance-stones followed feng-sacrifice form.

sentences.zh: 又為降禪壇於社首山上，方壇八隅，一成八陛，如方丘之制。

translations.literal: A descent-shan altar was also made on Sheshou Hill—a square altar with eight corners, one tier and eight steps, like the square mound form.
translations.idiomatic: A descent-shan altar on Sheshou Hill—square with eight corners, one tier, eight steps, like the square mound.

sentences.zh: 壇上飾以黃，四面依方色。

translations.literal: The altar top was adorned with yellow; the four sides followed directional colors.
translations.idiomatic: The altar top was yellow; sides followed directional colors.

sentences.zh: 三壝，隨地之宜。

translations.literal: Three enclosures, according to the terrain.
translations.idiomatic: Three enclosures, according to terrain.

sentences.zh: 其玉策、玉匱、石感、石檢、距石等，亦同封祀之制。

translations.literal: Jade slips, jade casket, stone receptacle, stone clasps, distance-stones, and the like also matched the feng-sacrifice form.
translations.idiomatic: Jade slips, jade casket, stone receptacle, stone clasps, and distance-stones matched feng-sacrifice form.

sentences.zh: 至其年十二月，車駕至山下。

translations.literal: By the twelfth month of that year the imperial carriage reached below the mountain.
translations.idiomatic: By month 12 the imperial carriage reached below the mountain.

sentences.zh: 及有司進奏儀注，封祀以高祖、太宗同配，禪社首乙太穆皇后、文德皇后同配，皆以公卿充亞獻、終獻之禮。

translations.literal: When the relevant offices submitted the ritual regulations, feng-sacrifice paired Gaozu and Taizong; shan at Sheshou paired Empress Tai Mu and Empress Wende; dukes and ministers served as secondary and final offerers.
translations.idiomatic: Offices submitted regulations: feng paired Gaozu and Taizong; Sheshou shan paired Empresses Tai Mu and Wende; dukes served as secondary and final offerers.

sentences.zh: 於是皇后抗表曰：

translations.literal: Thereupon the empress submitted a memorial:
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the empress submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 伏尋登封之禮，遠邁古先，而降禪之儀，竊為未允。

translations.literal: Reflecting on the rite of ascending feng, it far surpasses antiquity; yet the ceremony of descent shan, I venture, is not approved.
translations.idiomatic: Ascending feng far surpasses antiquity; yet descent shan, I venture, is not approved.

sentences.zh: 其祭地祇之日，以太后昭配，至於行事，皆以公卿。

translations.literal: On the day of sacrificing to Earth Sovereign, Empress Zhao was matched; in performing the rite, all were dukes and ministers.
translations.idiomatic: On Earth Sovereign's day Empress Zhao was matched; in the rite all were dukes and ministers.

sentences.zh: 以妾愚誠，恐未周備。

translations.literal: In my foolish sincerity, I fear it is not complete.
translations.idiomatic: In my foolish sincerity, I fear it is incomplete.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 乾坤定位，剛柔之義已殊；

translations.literal: Heaven and Earth are positioned; the meanings of firm and yielding already differ;
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and Earth are positioned; firm and yielding already differ;

sentences.zh: 經義載陳，中外之儀斯別。

translations.literal: the classics state it clearly; the ceremonies of inner and outer already differ.
translations.idiomatic: the classics state it clearly; inner and outer ceremonies differ.

sentences.zh: 瑤壇作配，既合于方祇；

translations.literal: Jade altar as matching already fits Earth Sovereign of the square;
translations.idiomatic: Jade altar as matching already fits square Earth Sovereign;

sentences.zh: 玉豆薦芳，實歸於內職。

translations.literal: jade vessels offering fragrance truly belong to inner duties.
translations.idiomatic: jade vessels offering fragrance truly belong to inner duties.

sentences.zh: 況推尊先後，親饗瓊筵，豈有外命宰臣，內參禋祭？

translations.literal: How much more in honoring predecessors and personally feasting at the jade banquet—could outer orders to ministers and inner participation in sacrifice coexist?
translations.idiomatic: Honoring predecessors at the jade banquet—could outer orders to ministers and inner sacrifice coexist?

sentences.zh: 詳於至理，有紊徽章。

translations.literal: Examined to ultimate principle, regulations are disordered.
translations.idiomatic: Examined to principle, regulations are disordered.

sentences.zh: 但禮節之源，雖興於昔典；

translations.literal: Yet though the source of ritual arose in ancient canons,
translations.idiomatic: Though ritual's source arose in ancient canons,

sentences.zh: 而升降之制，尚缺於遙圖。

translations.literal: the system of ascending and descending still lacks in distant plans.
translations.idiomatic: ascending and descending systems still lack in distant plans.

sentences.zh: 且往代封嶽，雖雲顯號，或因時俗，意在尋仙；

translations.literal: Moreover in former generations' fenging peaks, though they bore glorious titles, some followed custom and sought immortality;
translations.idiomatic: Former fenging sometimes sought glorious titles, followed custom, sought immortality;

sentences.zh: 或以情覬名，事深為己。

translations.literal: some coveted reputation from feeling, the affair deeply for oneself.
translations.idiomatic: some coveted reputation, the affair deeply for oneself.

sentences.zh: 豈如化被乎四表，推美于神宗；

translations.literal: How like transforming the four quarters and extending beauty to the divine ancestor;
translations.idiomatic: How unlike transforming the four quarters and extending beauty to the divine ancestor;

sentences.zh: 道冠乎二儀，歸功於先德。

translations.literal: the Way crowns the two principles and returns merit to former virtue.
translations.idiomatic: the Way crowns the two principles and returns merit to former virtue.

sentences.zh: 寧可仍遵舊軌，靡創彝章？

translations.literal: How could one still follow the old track and not create constant regulations?
translations.idiomatic: How follow the old track and not create constant regulations?

sentences.zh: 妾謬處椒闈，叨居蘭掖。

translations.literal: I wrongly occupy the pepper chambers and presumptuously dwell in the orchid side.
translations.idiomatic: I wrongly occupy the pepper chambers and dwell in the orchid side.

sentences.zh: 但以職惟中饋，道屬於蒸、嘗；

translations.literal: Yet my duty is only inner provision; the Way belongs to steaming and tasting;
translations.idiomatic: Yet my duty is inner provision; the Way belongs to steaming and tasting;

sentences.zh: 義切奉先，理光於蘋、藻。

translations.literal: the meaning of serving ancestors cuts to offering duckweed and water-shield.
translations.idiomatic: serving ancestors cuts to duckweed and water-shield offerings.

sentences.zh: 罔極之思，載結於因心；

translations.literal: Thought of boundlessness knots in the heart;
translations.idiomatic: Boundless thought knots in the heart;

sentences.zh: 祗肅之懷，實深於明祀。

translations.literal: reverent solemnity in mind runs deep for bright sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: reverent solemnity runs deep for bright sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 但妾早乖定省，已闕侍於晨昏；

translations.literal: Yet I early lost morning and evening attendance and already lack serving at dawn and dusk;
translations.idiomatic: Yet I early lost dawn-and-dusk attendance;

sentences.zh: 今屬崇禋，豈敢安於帷帟。

translations.literal: now facing great sacrifice, how dare I rest within curtains?
translations.idiomatic: now facing great sacrifice, how dare I rest within curtains?

sentences.zh: 是故馳情夕寢，睠嬴裏而翹魂；

translations.literal: Therefore my feelings race at evening rest, soul straining toward the inner palace;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore feelings race at evening rest, soul straining toward the inner palace;

sentences.zh: 疊慮宵興，仰深郊而聳念。

translations.literal: thoughts layer at night rising, head lifted to the deep suburb in remembrance.
translations.idiomatic: thoughts layer at night rising, lifted to the deep suburb in remembrance.

sentences.zh: 伏望展禮之日，總率六宮內外命婦，以親奉奠。

translations.literal: I humbly hope on the day the rites unfold to lead the six palaces, inner and outer titled women, to offer in person.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly hope on rite day to lead six palaces and titled women to offer in person.

sentences.zh: 冀申如在之敬，式展虔拜之儀。

translations.literal: May it extend 'as if present' reverence and unfold sincere bowing ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: May it extend 'as if present' reverence and unfold sincere bowing.

sentences.zh: 積此微誠，已淹氣序。

translations.literal: Gathering this slight sincerity has already spanned seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Gathering this slight sincerity has spanned seasons.

sentences.zh: 既屬鑾輿將警，奠璧非賒，輒效丹心，庶裨大禮。

translations.literal: Now that the imperial carriage will soon depart, offering jade cannot delay; I venture my loyal heart, hoping to aid the great rite.
translations.idiomatic: The carriage will soon depart; offering jade cannot delay—I venture loyal heart to aid the great rite.

sentences.zh: 冀聖朝垂則，永播於芳規；

translations.literal: May the sagely court set precedent and spread forever in fragrant regulation;
translations.idiomatic: May the sagely court set precedent and spread fragrant regulation;

sentences.zh: 螢燭末光，增輝於日月。

translations.literal: firefly and candle's last light add radiance to sun and moon.
translations.idiomatic: firefly light add radiance to sun and moon.

sentences.zh: 於是祭地祇、梁甫，皆以皇后為亞獻，諸王大妃為終獻。

translations.literal: Thereupon in sacrificing to Earth Sovereign and at Liangfu, the empress served as secondary offerer and the great consorts of princes as final offerers.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon at Earth Sovereign and Liangfu sacrifice, the empress was secondary offerer and princes' great consorts final offerers.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，前羅文府果毅李敬貞論封禪須明水實樽：「《淮南子》云：'方諸見月，則津而為水。

translations.literal: On bingchen, former Luowen-fu Guoyi officer Li Jingzhen discussed that feng and shan require clear water in solid vessels: "The Huainanzi says: 'When the square zhū meets the moon, moisture becomes water.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, former Guoyi officer Li Jingzhen argued feng-shan needs clear water in solid vessels: "The Huainanzi says, 'When the square zhū meets the moon, moisture becomes water.

sentences.zh: '高誘注云：'方諸，陰燧，大蛤也。

translations.literal: Commentator Gao You says: 'The square zhū is the yin fire-drill—a large clam.
translations.idiomatic: Gao You comments, 'The square zhū is the yin fire-drill—a large clam.

sentences.zh: 熟摩拭令熱，以向月，則水生。

translations.literal: Rubbed hot when cooked, turned toward the moon, then water forms.
translations.idiomatic: Rubbed hot when cooked and turned toward the moon, water forms.

sentences.zh: 以銅盤受之，下數石。

translations.literal: A bronze basin receives it—several stone's worth below.
translations.idiomatic: A bronze basin receives it—several stone below.

sentences.zh: '王充《論衡》云：'陽燧取火于日，方諸取水於月，相去甚遠，而火至水來者，氣感之驗也。

translations.literal: Wang Chong's Lunheng says: 'The yang fire-drill takes fire from the sun; the square zhū takes water from the moon—far apart, yet fire comes and water comes: the verification of qi resonance.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chong's Lunheng says, 'The yang fire-drill takes fire from the sun; the square zhū takes water from the moon—far apart, yet fire and water come: qi resonance verified.

sentences.zh: '《漢舊儀》云：'八月飲酎，車駕夕牲，以鑒諸取水於月，以陽燧取火於日。

translations.literal: The Han Old Ceremonies say: 'In the eighth month, drinking the lees-wine, the carriage at evening sacrifice, uses the mirror-zhū to take water from the moon and the yang fire-drill to take fire from the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Han Old Ceremonies say, 'Eighth month lees-wine: at evening sacrifice the carriage uses mirror-zhū for moon water and yang fire-drill for sun fire.

sentences.zh: '《周禮·考工記》云：'金有六齊。

translations.literal: The Zhouli, Artificers' Record says: 'Metal has six alloys.
translations.idiomatic: Zhouli Artificers' Record says, 'Metal has six alloys.

sentences.zh: 金錫半，謂之鑒燧之齊。

translations.literal: Half gold half tin is called the alloy of mirror and fire-drill.
translations.idiomatic: Half gold half tin is mirror-and-fire-drill alloy.

sentences.zh: '鄭玄注云：'鑒燧，取水火於日月之器也。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan's comment says: 'Mirror and fire-drill are vessels for taking water and fire from sun and moon.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan comments, 'Mirror and fire-drill take water and fire from sun and moon.

sentences.zh: '准鄭此注，則水火之器，皆以金錫為之。

translations.literal: Following Zheng's comment, fire and water vessels are all made of gold and tin.
translations.idiomatic: By Zheng's comment, fire and water vessels are gold-tin.

sentences.zh: 今司宰有陽燧，形如圓鏡，以取明火；

translations.literal: Now the chief steward has a yang fire-drill, round mirror in form, to obtain bright fire;
translations.idiomatic: The chief steward has a yang fire-drill, round mirror-shaped, for bright fire;

sentences.zh: 陰鑒形如方鏡，以取明水。

translations.literal: the yin mirror is square mirror in form, to obtain clear water.
translations.idiomatic: the yin mirror is square, for clear water.

sentences.zh: 但比年祠祭，皆用陽燧取火，應時得；

translations.literal: But in recent years' temple sacrifices all use the yang fire-drill for fire and obtain it in season;
translations.idiomatic: Recent sacrifices use the yang fire-drill for fire in season;

sentences.zh: 以陰鑒取水，未有得者，常用井水替明水之處。」

translations.literal: using the yin mirror for water, none has obtained it—well water is commonly substituted where clear water is needed."
translations.idiomatic: the yin mirror for water has never worked—well water substitutes for clear water.'"

sentences.zh: 奉敕令禮司研究。

translations.literal: By imperial order the ritual office was told to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial order the ritual office investigated.

sentences.zh: 敬貞因說先儒是非，言及明水，乃云：「周禮金錫相半，自是造陽燧法，鄭玄錯解以為陰鑒之制。

translations.literal: Jingzhen, explaining former scholars' right and wrong and speaking of clear water, then said: "Zhouli's half gold half tin is itself the method for making the yang fire-drill; Zheng Xuan wrongly interpreted it as the yin mirror's form.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhen, on clear water, said, "Zhouli's half gold half tin is the yang fire-drill method; Zheng Xuan wrongly took it for the yin mirror.

sentences.zh: 仍古取明水法，合用方諸，引《淮南子》等書，用大蛤也。」

translations.literal: Still the ancient method for taking clear water should use the square zhū; citing the Huainanzi and other books, a large clam is used."
translations.idiomatic: Ancient clear-water method should use the square zhū; Huainanzi and others use a large clam.'"

sentences.zh: 又稱：「敬貞曾八九月中，取蛤一尺二寸者依法試之。

translations.literal: He also stated: "Jingzhen once in the eighth or ninth month took a clam one chi two cun and tested by the method.
translations.idiomatic: He also stated, "Jingzhen once in month 8 or 9 took a one chi two cun clam and tested by method.

sentences.zh: 自人定至夜半，得水四五斗。」

translations.literal: From rending to midnight he obtained four or five dou of water."
translations.idiomatic: From rending to midnight he obtained four or five dou of water.'"

sentences.zh: 奉常奏曰：「封禪祭祀，即須明水實樽。

translations.literal: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices memorialized: "Feng and shan sacrifice immediately requires clear water in solid vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Court of Sacrifices memorialized, "Feng-shan sacrifice needs clear water in solid vessels.

sentences.zh: 敬貞所陳，檢有故實。」

translations.literal: What Jingzhen stated, on examination has precedent."
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhen's statement has precedent on examination.'"

sentences.zh: 又稱：「先經試驗確執，望請差敬貞自取蚌蛤，便赴太山與所司對試。」

translations.literal: It also stated: having been tested and firmly held, we hope Jingzhen may be dispatched to take clams himself and go to Mount Tai to test against the relevant offices."
translations.idiomatic: It also stated: "Tested and firmly held—we hope Jingzhen may take clams and test at Mount Tai with the offices."

sentences.zh: 是日，制曰：「古今典制，文質不同，至於制度，隨世代沿革，唯祀天地，獨不改張，斯乃自處於厚，奉天以薄。

translations.literal: That day an edict said: "Ancient and modern canonical forms differ in substance and ornament; as for institutions, they change with generations—only sacrificing to Heaven and Earth has not been altered; this is placing oneself thickly while serving Heaven thinly.
translations.idiomatic: That day an edict said, "Ancient and modern forms differ in substance and ornament; institutions change with generations—only Heaven-and-Earth sacrifice is unchanged: thick self, thin Heaven.

sentences.zh: 又今封禪，即用玉牒金繩，器物之間，復有瓦樽秸席，一時行禮，文質頓乖，駁而不倫，深為未愜。

translations.literal: Moreover today's feng and shan uses jade tablets and gold cord; among vessels there are again earthen vessels, straw mats, and gourd cups—performing the rite at once, substance and ornament suddenly clash, mixed and unharmonious, deeply unsatisfying.
translations.idiomatic: Today's feng-shan uses jade and gold cord yet also earthen vessels, straw mats, gourd cups—substance and ornament clash, deeply unsatisfying.

sentences.zh: 其封祀、降禪所設上帝、後土位，先設颭秸、瓦甒、瓢杯等物，並宜改用裀褥罍爵，每事從文。

translations.literal: At the seats of Lord on High and Queen Earth in feng-sacrifice and descent-shan, items first set out such as fluttering straw, earthen jars, and gourd cups should all be changed to cushions, mats, urns, and goblets—each matter following ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Lord on High and Queen Earth seats in feng and descent-shan: replace fluttering straw, earthen jars, gourd cups with cushions, urns, goblets—each matter ornamented.

sentences.zh: 其諸郊祀，亦宜准此。」

translations.literal: Other suburban sacrifices should also follow this."
translations.idiomatic: Other suburban sacrifices should follow.'"

sentences.zh: 於是昊天上帝之座褥以蒼，皇地祇褥以黃，配帝及後褥以紫，五方上帝及大明、夜明席皆以方色，內官已下席皆以莞。

translations.literal: Thereupon August Heaven's seat cushion was dark blue, Imperial Earth Sovereign's yellow, matched lords and consorts purple; Five Directional Lords and Great Brightness and Night Brightness mats followed directional colors; inner officials' mats and below were all cattail.
translations.idiomatic: August Heaven's cushion was dark blue, Earth Sovereign's yellow, matched lords purple; Five Directional Lords and Brightness mats followed colors; inner officials' mats were cattail.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，帝親享昊天上帝於山下，封禮之壇，如圓丘之儀。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year the emperor personally offered to August Heaven below the mountain at the feng-sacrifice altar, as in the round mound rite.
translations.idiomatic: Month 1, year 3, the emperor personally offered to August Heaven below at the feng altar, as at the round mound.

sentences.zh: 祭訖，親封玉策，置石感，聚五色土封之。

translations.literal: When sacrifice ended, he personally sealed jade slips, placed the stone receptacle, and heaped five-colored earth to seal it.
translations.idiomatic: When sacrifice ended, he sealed jade slips, placed the stone receptacle, and heaped five-colored earth.

sentences.zh: 圓徑一丈二尺，高九尺。

translations.literal: Round diameter one zhang two chi, height nine chi.
translations.idiomatic: Round diameter one zhang two chi, height nine chi.

sentences.zh: 其日，帝率侍臣已下升泰山。

translations.literal: That day the emperor led attendants and below up Mount Tai.
translations.idiomatic: That day the emperor led attendants up Mount Tai.

sentences.zh: 翌日，就山上登封之壇封玉策訖，復還山下之齋宮。

translations.literal: The next day, at the ascent-feng altar atop the mountain he finished sealing the jade slips and returned to the abstention palace below.
translations.idiomatic: Next day at the ascent-feng altar he finished sealing jade slips and returned to the abstention palace below.

sentences.zh: 其明日，親祀皇地祇於社首山上，降禪之壇，如方丘之儀。

translations.literal: The day after, he personally sacrificed to Imperial Earth Sovereign on Sheshou Hill at the descent-shan altar, as in the square mound rite.
translations.idiomatic: The day after, he sacrificed to Imperial Earth Sovereign on Sheshou at the descent-shan altar, as at the square mound.

sentences.zh: 皇后為亞獻，越國太妃燕氏為終獻。

translations.literal: The empress was secondary offerer; Princess of Yue great consort Lady Yan was final offerer.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was secondary offerer; Yue Princess great consort Lady Yan final offerer.

sentences.zh: 翌日，上御朝覲壇以朝群臣，如元日之儀。

translations.literal: The next day the emperor attended the Grand Audience altar to hold court with ministers, as on New Year's Day.
translations.idiomatic: Next day the emperor held court at the Grand Audience altar as on New Year's Day.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，宴文武百僚，大赦改元。

translations.literal: When rites ended, he feasted civil and military officials and proclaimed a great amnesty and changed the era name.
translations.idiomatic: Rites ended; he feasted officials, proclaimed great amnesty, and changed the era name.

sentences.zh: 初，上親享於降禪之壇，行初獻之禮畢，執事者皆趨而下。

translations.literal: At first, when the emperor personally offered at the descent-shan altar and the initial offering was finished, the officiants all hurried down.
translations.idiomatic: At first, after the initial offering at descent-shan, officiants hurried down.

sentences.zh: 宦者執帷，皇后率六宮以升，行禮。

translations.literal: Eunuchs held curtains; the empress led the six palaces up to perform the rite.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs held curtains; the empress led the six palaces up to perform the rite.

sentences.zh: 帷帟皆以錦繡為之。

translations.literal: Curtains were all made of brocade.
translations.idiomatic: Curtains were all brocade.

sentences.zh: 百僚在位瞻望，或竊議焉。

translations.literal: Officials in position gazed up; some whispered privately.
translations.idiomatic: Officials gazed up; some whispered privately.

sentences.zh: 於是詔立登封、降禪、朝覲之碑，各於壇所。

translations.literal: Thereupon edicts ordered steles for ascent-feng, descent-shan, and grand audience, each at its altar.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts ordered steles for ascent-feng, descent-shan, and grand audience at each altar.

sentences.zh: 又詔名封祀壇為舞鶴台，介丘壇為萬歲台，降禪壇為景雲台，以紀當時所見之瑞焉。

translations.literal: Edicts also named the feng-sacrifice altar Dancing Crane Terrace, Jie Hill altar Myriad Years Terrace, descent-shan altar Auspicious Cloud Terrace, to record the omens seen at the time.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts named feng altar Dancing Crane Terrace, Jie Hill altar Myriad Years Terrace, descent-shan altar Auspicious Cloud Terrace, recording omens.

sentences.zh: 高宗既封泰山之後，又欲遍封五嶽。

translations.literal: After Gaozong had fenged Mount Tai, he also wished to feng all five peaks in turn.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozong fenged Mount Tai, he wished to feng all five peaks.

sentences.zh: 至永淳元年，於洛州嵩山之南，置崇陽縣。

translations.literal: By the first year of Yongchun, south of Mount Song in Luozhou, Chongyang County was established.
translations.idiomatic: Yongchun 1, south of Mount Song in Luozhou, Chongyang County was established.

sentences.zh: 其年七月，敕其所造奉天宮。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of that year he ordered construction of Fengtian Palace there.
translations.idiomatic: Month 7 that year he ordered Fengtian Palace built there.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，駕幸奉天宮。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year the carriage visited Fengtian Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year, the carriage visited Fengtian Palace.

sentences.zh: 至七月，下詔將以其年十一月封禪于嵩嶽。

translations.literal: By the seventh month an edict was issued that in the eleventh month of that year feng and shan would be performed at Mount Song.
translations.idiomatic: Month 7 an edict announced feng and shan at Mount Song in month 11 that year.

sentences.zh: 詔國子司業李行偉、考工員外郎賈大隱、太常博士韋叔夏裴守貞輔抱素等詳定儀注。

translations.literal: The edict ordered Directorate of Education Vice Director Li Xingwei, Works Section Vice Director Jia Dayin, and Court of Imperial Sacrifices Erudites Wei Shuxia, Pei Shouzhen, and Fu Baosu to fix the ritual regulations in detail.
translations.idiomatic: The edict ordered Li Xingwei, Jia Dayin, and erudites Wei Shuxia, Pei Shouzhen, and Fu Baosu to fix regulations.

sentences.zh: 於是議：

translations.literal: Thereupon they proposed:
translations.idiomatic: They proposed:

sentences.zh: 立封祀壇，如圓丘之制。

translations.literal: Establish a feng-sacrifice altar like the round mound form.
translations.idiomatic: Establish a feng-sacrifice altar like the round mound.

sentences.zh: 上飾以玄，四面依方色。

translations.literal: The top adorned with black; the four sides follow directional colors.
translations.idiomatic: Top black; four sides follow directional colors.

sentences.zh: 為圓壇，三成，高二丈四尺，每等高六尺。

translations.literal: Make a round altar, three tiers, two zhang four chi high total, each tier six chi high.
translations.idiomatic: Round altar, three tiers, two zhang four chi total, six chi per tier.

sentences.zh: 壇上徑一十六步，三等各闊四步。

translations.literal: Altar top diameter sixteen paces; each tier four paces wide.
translations.idiomatic: Top diameter sixteen paces; each tier four paces wide.

sentences.zh: 設十二陛，陛皆上闊八尺，下闊一丈四尺。

translations.literal: Set twelve flights of steps; each flight eight chi wide above, one zhang four chi below.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve flights; eight chi wide above, one zhang four chi below.

sentences.zh: 為三重壝，距外壝三十步，內壝距五十步。

translations.literal: Make triple enclosures; outer enclosure thirty paces out, inner fifty paces.
translations.idiomatic: Triple enclosures; outer thirty paces out, inner fifty.

sentences.zh: 燎壇在壇東南外壝之內，高三尺，方一丈五尺，南出陛。

translations.literal: Firewood altar southeast within the outer enclosure, three chi high, one zhang five chi square, steps south.
translations.idiomatic: Firewood altar southeast within outer enclosure, three chi high, one zhang five chi square, south steps.

sentences.zh: 登封壇，圓徑五丈，高九尺。

translations.literal: Ascent-feng altar, round diameter five zhang, nine chi high.
translations.idiomatic: Ascent-feng altar, five zhang diameter, nine chi high.

sentences.zh: 四出陛，為一壝，飾以五色，准封祀。

translations.literal: Steps on four sides, one enclosure, adorned with five colors, following feng-sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Four flights, one enclosure, five colors, following feng-sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 禪祭壇，上飾以金，四面依方色，為八角方壇，再成，高一丈二尺，每等高四尺。

translations.literal: Shan-sacrifice altar, top adorned with gold; four sides follow directional colors; eight-cornered square altar, two tiers, one zhang two chi total, four chi per tier.
translations.idiomatic: Shan altar, gold top; eight-cornered square, two tiers, one zhang two chi total, four chi per tier.

sentences.zh: 壇上方十六步，每等廣四步，設八陛。

translations.literal: Altar top sixteen paces square; each tier four paces wide; eight flights set.
translations.idiomatic: Top sixteen paces; each tier four paces; eight flights.

sentences.zh: 其上壇陛皆廣八尺，中等陛皆廣一丈，下等陛皆廣一丈二尺。

translations.literal: Upper-tier flights eight chi wide; middle-tier flights one zhang; lower-tier flights one zhang two chi.
translations.idiomatic: Upper flights eight chi; middle one zhang; lower one zhang two chi.

sentences.zh: 為三重壝之大小，准封祀。

translations.literal: Triple enclosures' sizes follow feng-sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Triple enclosures follow feng-sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 為埋坎，在壇之未地外壝之內，方深取足容物，南出陛。

translations.literal: Make a burial pit at the altar's lower ground within the outer enclosure, square and deep enough to hold objects, steps south.
translations.idiomatic: Burial pit at altar foot within outer enclosure, square, deep enough, south steps.

sentences.zh: 朝覲壇，於行宮之前為壇。

translations.literal: Grand Audience altar—make an altar before the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Audience altar before the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 宮方三分。

translations.literal: Palace in three parts.
translations.idiomatic: Palace in three parts.

sentences.zh: 壝二，在南。

translations.literal: Two enclosures, south.
translations.idiomatic: Two enclosures, south.

sentences.zh: 壇方二十四丈，高九尺，南面兩陛，餘三百各一陛。

translations.literal: Altar twenty-four zhang square, nine chi high; two flights south, one flight each on the other three hundred sides.
translations.idiomatic: Altar twenty-four zhang square, nine chi high; two south flights, one each elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 封祀、登封，五色土封石感為圓封，上徑一丈二尺，下徑三丈，高九尺。

translations.literal: Feng-sacrifice and ascent-feng: five-colored earth seals the stone receptacle as round feng, top diameter one zhang two chi, bottom three zhang, nine chi high.
translations.idiomatic: Feng and ascent: five-colored earth round seal on stone receptacle, top one zhang two chi, bottom three zhang, nine chi high.

sentences.zh: 禪祭，五色土封為八角方封，大小准封祀制度。

translations.literal: Shan sacrifice: five-colored earth seal as eight-cornered square, size following feng-sacrifice regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Shan: five-colored eight-cornered square seal, size per feng-sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 所用尺寸，准曆東封，並用古尺。

translations.literal: Dimensions used follow the eastern feng precedent and all use ancient chi.
translations.idiomatic: Dimensions follow eastern feng and ancient chi.

sentences.zh: 諸壇並築土為之，禮無用石之文。

translations.literal: All altars are built of earth; the rites have no text on using stone.
translations.idiomatic: All altars earth-built; rites have no stone.

sentences.zh: 並度影以定方位。

translations.literal: Shadow is also measured to fix orientation.
translations.idiomatic: Shadow measured to fix orientation.

sentences.zh: 登封、降禪，四出陛各當四方之中，陛各上廣七尺，下廣一丈二尺。

translations.literal: Ascent-feng and descent-shan: four flights each at the center of a direction; each flight seven chi wide above, one zhang two chi below.
translations.idiomatic: Ascent and descent: four center flights, seven chi above, one zhang two chi below.

sentences.zh: 封祀玉帛料，有蒼璧，四圭有邸，圭璧。

translations.literal: Feng-sacrifice jade and silk materials: dark blue bi, four gui with base, gui-bi.
translations.idiomatic: Feng jade and silk: dark blue bi, four gui with base, gui-bi.

sentences.zh: 禪祭有黃琮，兩圭有邸，無圭璧。

translations.literal: Shan sacrifice has yellow cong, two gui with base, no gui-bi.
translations.idiomatic: Shan has yellow cong, two gui with base, no gui-bi.

sentences.zh: 又定登封、降禪、朝覲等日。

translations.literal: They also fixed days for ascent-feng, descent-shan, and grand audience.
translations.idiomatic: They also fixed days for ascent-feng, descent-shan, and audience.

sentences.zh: 准禮，冬至祭天於圓丘，其封祀請用十二日。

translations.literal: Following the rites, winter solstice sacrifices Heaven at the round mound; feng-sacrifice is requested on the twelfth day.
translations.idiomatic: Per rites, solstice sacrifices Heaven at round mound; feng-sacrifice on day 12.

sentences.zh: 准東封祀故事，十二日登封，十三日禪祭，十四日朝覲。

translations.literal: Following eastern feng-sacrifice precedent: twelfth day ascent-feng, thirteenth shan, fourteenth audience.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern precedent: day 12 ascent, 13 shan, 14 audience.

sentences.zh: 若有故，須改登封已下期日，在禮無妨。

translations.literal: If there is cause to change days after ascent-feng, the rites permit no harm.
translations.idiomatic: Changing days after ascent is permitted if needed.

sentences.zh: 又輦輿料云：封祀、登封，皇帝出乘玉輅，還乘金輅。

translations.literal: Carriage materials also state: for feng-sacrifice and ascent-feng the emperor departs in the jade carriage and returns in the gold carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Carriage materials: feng and ascent—depart jade carriage, return gold.

sentences.zh: 皇太子往還金輅。

translations.literal: Crown prince goes and returns in gold carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Crown prince goes and returns gold carriage.

sentences.zh: 禪祭，皇帝、太子如封祀。

translations.literal: Shan sacrifice: emperor and crown prince as in feng-sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Shan: emperor and crown prince as feng-sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 又衣服料云：「東封祠祭日，天皇服袞冕，近奉制，依《貞觀禮》服大裘。

translations.literal: Clothing materials also state: "On eastern feng sacrifice days the sovereign wears dragon robe; recently by edict, follow Zhenguan Rites in wearing great fur robe.
translations.idiomatic: Clothing materials: "Eastern feng days sovereign wears dragon robe; recently by edict, Zhenguan Rites great fur robe.

sentences.zh: 又云：袞冕服一具，齋服之；

translations.literal: It also states: one set dragon robe for abstention;
translations.idiomatic: Also: one dragon robe set for abstention;

sentences.zh: 通天冠服一具，回服之；

translations.literal: one set Tongtian crown robe for return;
translations.idiomatic: one Tongtian crown set for return;

sentences.zh: 翼善冠服一具，馬上服之。

translations.literal: one set Yishan crown robe for riding.
translations.idiomatic: one Yishan crown set for riding.

sentences.zh: 皇太子袞冕服。

translations.literal: Crown prince dragon robe.
translations.idiomatic: Crown prince dragon robe.

sentences.zh: 又齋則服遠遊冠，受朝則公服遠遊冠服，馬上則進德冠服。」

translations.literal: In abstention wear far-travel crown; in receiving audience wear duke's far-travel crown; on horse wear Jinde crown."
translations.idiomatic: Abstention: far-travel crown; audience: duke's far-travel crown; horse: Jinde crown."

sentences.zh: 當時又令詳求射牛之禮。

translations.literal: At the time they also ordered detailed inquiry into the rite of shooting the ox.
translations.idiomatic: They also ordered inquiry into shooting the ox.

sentences.zh: 行偉、守貞等議曰：「據《周禮》及《國語》，郊祀天地，天子自射其牲。

translations.literal: Xingwei, Shouzhen, and others proposed: "According to the Zhouli and Discourses of the States, in suburban sacrifice to Heaven and Earth the Son of Heaven personally shoots the victim.
translations.idiomatic: Xingwei and Shouzhen proposed: "Zhouli and Discourses: suburban Heaven-and-Earth sacrifice—the Son of Heaven shoots the victim.

sentences.zh: 漢武唯封太山，令侍中儒者射牛行事。

translations.literal: Han Wudi only fenged Mount Tai and ordered attendant gentlemen and Confucians to shoot the ox in performing the rite.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi only fenged Tai and ordered attendants and Confucians to shoot the ox.

sentences.zh: 至於餘祀，亦無射牲之文。

translations.literal: As for other sacrifices, there is also no text on shooting victims.
translations.idiomatic: Other sacrifices have no shooting text.

sentences.zh: 但親舂射牲，雖是古禮，久從廢省。

translations.literal: But personally pounding grain and shooting victims, though ancient rites, have long been reduced and omitted.
translations.idiomatic: Personal pounding and shooting, though ancient, long omitted.

sentences.zh: 據封禪禮，祀日，未明十五刻，宰人以鑾刀割牲，質明而行事。

translations.literal: According to feng-shan rites, on sacrifice day at fifteen quarters before dawn the butcher cuts the victim with the imperial knife; at full dawn the rite proceeds.
translations.idiomatic: Feng-shan: fifteen quarters before dawn butcher cuts with imperial knife; full dawn rite proceeds.

sentences.zh: 比鑾駕至時，牢牲總畢，天皇唯奠玉酌獻而已。

translations.literal: By the time the imperial carriage arrives, victims are all finished; the sovereign only sets jade and pours offering.
translations.idiomatic: When the carriage arrives victims are done; sovereign only sets jade and pours.

sentences.zh: 今若祀前一日射牲，事即傷早。

translations.literal: If shooting the victim the day before sacrifice, the affair is too early.
translations.idiomatic: Shooting day before is too early.

sentences.zh: 祀日方始射牲，事又傷晚。

translations.literal: If shooting at sacrifice day, the affair is too late.
translations.idiomatic: Shooting on sacrifice day is too late.

sentences.zh: 若依漢武故事，即非親射之儀，事不可行。」

translations.literal: If following Wudi's story, it is not the ceremony of personal shooting—the affair cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: Following Wudi is not personal shooting—the affair cannot be done.'"

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict followed this.
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed.

sentences.zh: 尋屬高宗不豫，遂罷封禪之禮。

translations.literal: Soon Gaozong fell ill and the feng-shan rites were abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Gaozong fell ill and feng-shan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 則天證聖元年，將有事於嵩山，先遣使致祭以祈福助，下制，號嵩山為神嶽，尊嵩山神為天中王，夫人為靈妃。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhensheng, when there would be affairs at Mount Song, envoys were first sent to sacrifice and pray for blessing; an edict titled Mount Song Divine Peak and honored the Mount Song spirit as King of Heaven's Center, his consort as Spirit Consort.
translations.idiomatic: Zhensheng 1, envoys sacrificed at Mount Song for blessing; Mount Song titled Divine Peak, spirit as King of Heaven's Center, consort Spirit Consort.

sentences.zh: 嵩山舊有夏啟及啟母、少室阿姨神廟，咸令預祈祭。

translations.literal: Mount Song formerly had shrines to Xia Qi, Qi's mother, and Young Chamber Aunt Spirit; all were included in prayer sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Former shrines to Xia Qi, Qi's mother, and Young Chamber Aunt were included.

sentences.zh: 至天冊萬歲二年臘月甲申，親行登封之禮。

translations.literal: By the twelfth month, day jiashen, of the second year of Tiance Wansui, she personally performed the ascent-feng rite.
translations.idiomatic: Tiance Wansui 2, month 12, day jiashen, she personally performed ascent-feng.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，便大赦，改元萬歲登封，改嵩陽縣為登封縣，陽成縣為告成縣。

translations.literal: When rites ended, she immediately proclaimed great amnesty, changed the era to Wansui Dengfeng, renamed Songyang County Dengfeng County and Yangcheng County Gaocheng County.
translations.idiomatic: Rites ended; great amnesty; era Wansui Dengfeng; Songyang to Dengfeng, Yangcheng to Gaocheng.

sentences.zh: 粵三日丁亥，禪於少室山。

translations.literal: On the third day dinghai she shaned at Mount Shaoshi.
translations.idiomatic: Day 3 dinghai she shaned at Mount Shaoshi.

sentences.zh: 又二日己丑，禦朝覲壇朝群臣，咸如乾封之儀。

translations.literal: Two days later on jichou she attended the Grand Audience altar and held court with ministers, all as in Qianfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later jichou she held audience as in Qianfeng.

sentences.zh: 則天以封禪日為嵩嶽神祇所祐，遂尊神岳天中王為神岳天中皇帝，靈妃為天中皇后，夏後啟為齊聖皇帝；

translations.literal: Wu Zetian, because feng-shan day was aided by Mount Song's spirits, then honored Divine Peak King of Heaven's Center as Divine Peak Emperor of Heaven's Center and Spirit Consort as Empress of Heaven's Center; Xia Hou Qi as Sagely Emperor;
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zetian honored Divine Peak King as Divine Peak Emperor of Heaven's Center, Spirit Consort as Empress of Heaven's Center; Xia Qi as Sagely Emperor;

sentences.zh: 封啟母神為玉京太后，少室阿姨神為金闕夫人；

translations.literal: honored Qi's mother Spirit as Jade Capital Empress Dowager and Young Chamber Aunt Spirit as Golden Portal Lady;
translations.idiomatic: Qi's mother as Jade Capital Empress Dowager, Young Chamber Aunt as Golden Portal Lady;

sentences.zh: 王子晉為升仙太子，別為立廟。

translations.literal: Prince Zijin as Ascendant Immortal Crown Prince, with a separate shrine established.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zijin as Ascendant Immortal Crown Prince, separate shrine.

sentences.zh: 登封壇南有槲樹，大赦日於其杪置金雞樹。

translations.literal: South of the ascent-feng altar was an oak tree; on amnesty day a golden rooster tree was placed in its crown.
translations.idiomatic: South of ascent altar was an oak; on amnesty day a golden rooster tree in its crown.

sentences.zh: 則天自製《升中述志碑》，樹於壇之丙地。

translations.literal: Wu Zetian herself composed the Stele of Ascent Expressing Intent and set it at the altar's bing site.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zetian composed the Stele of Ascent Expressing Intent at the altar's bing site.

sentences.zh: 玄宗開元十二年，文武百僚、朝集使、皇親及四方文學之士，皆以理化升平，時穀屢稔，上書請修封禪之禮並獻賦頌者，前後千有餘篇。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Kaiyuan, civil and military officials, assembly envoys, imperial kin, and literary men from all quarters—all because governance and transformation had risen and grain was repeatedly abundant—submitted memorials requesting feng-shan rites and presented fu and eulogies, more than a thousand in all.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyuan 12, officials and literati memorialized for feng-shan and presented fu and eulogies—over a thousand.

sentences.zh: 玄宗謙沖不許。

translations.literal: Xuanzong modestly refused.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong modestly refused.

sentences.zh: 中書令張說又累日固請，乃下制曰：

translations.literal: Central Secretariat Director Zhang Yue again firmly requested for many days; then an edict was issued:
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue firmly requested for days; then an edict:

sentences.zh: 自古受命而王者，曷嘗不封泰山，禪梁父，答厚德，告成功。

translations.literal: From antiquity, rulers who received the Mandate—who has not fenged Mount Tai, shaned at Liangfu, answered thick virtue, and announced success?
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity, who received the Mandate without fenging Tai, shaning Liangfu, answering virtue, announcing success?

sentences.zh: 三代之前，罔不由此。

translations.literal: Before the Three Dynasties, none failed to do so.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Three Dynasties, none failed.

sentences.zh: 越自魏、晉，以迄周、隋，帝典闕而大道隱，王綱弛而舊章缺，千載寂寥，封崇莫嗣。

translations.literal: From Wei and Jin through Zhou and Sui, imperial canons were lacking and the great Way hidden, royal net slack and old regulations missing—a thousand years of silence, feng and honor without succession.
translations.idiomatic: From Wei-Jin through Zhou-Sui, canons lacked, the Way hid, regulations missed—a thousand years without succession.

sentences.zh: 物極而復，天祚我唐，武、文二後，應圖受籙。

translations.literal: When things reach extremity they return; Heaven bestowed our Tang; Emperors Wu and Wen answered the chart and received the tally.
translations.idiomatic: At extremity, return; Heaven bestowed Tang; Wu and Wen received the tally.

sentences.zh: 洎于高宗，重光累盛，承至理，登介丘，懷百神，震六合，紹殷、周之統，接虞、夏之風。

translations.literal: Down to Gaozong, repeated glory and abundance, inheriting ultimate principle, ascending Jie Hill, embracing the hundred spirits, shaking the six quarters, continuing Yin and Zhou's succession, joining Yu and Xia's wind.
translations.idiomatic: To Gaozong: repeated glory, ultimate principle, Jie Hill, hundred spirits, six quarters, Yin-Zhou succession, Yu-Xia wind.

sentences.zh: 中宗弘懿鑠之休，睿宗沐粹精之道，巍巍蕩蕩，無得而稱者也。

translations.literal: Zhongzong's splendid blessings, Ruizong bathed in pure essence—the towering, the vast, beyond naming.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong's blessings, Ruizong's essence—towering, vast, beyond naming.

sentences.zh: 朕昔戡多難，稟略先朝，虔奉慈旨，嗣膺丕業。

translations.literal: I formerly quelled many hardships, received forebear's strategy, reverently followed kind intent, and succeeded to the great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: I quelled hardships, received forebear strategy, followed kind intent, succeeded enterprise.

sentences.zh: 是用創九廟以申孝敬，禮二郊以展嚴禋，寶菽粟於水火，捐珠玉於山谷。

translations.literal: Therefore I established the nine temples to extend filial reverence, performed the two suburbs to unfold solemn sacrifice, treasured grain above fire and water, cast pearls and jade into valleys.
translations.idiomatic: I established nine temples, performed two suburbs, treasured grain, cast pearls into valleys.

sentences.zh: 兢兢業業，非敢追美前王；

translations.literal: Diligent and cautious—I dare not chase former kings' beauty;
translations.idiomatic: Diligent—I dare not chase former kings;

sentences.zh: 日慎一日，實以奉遵遺訓。

translations.literal: daily cautious—I truly follow the departed instruction.
translations.idiomatic: daily cautious—I follow departed instruction.

sentences.zh: 至於巡狩大典，封禪鴻名，顧惟寡薄，未遑時邁，十四載於茲矣。

translations.literal: As for the great canon of tour and hunt, the great name of feng-shan—considering my meager thinness, I have not yet had leisure to advance in season; fourteen years have passed.
translations.idiomatic: The tour canon and feng-shan name—I, meager, have not advanced; fourteen years passed.

sentences.zh: 今百谷有年，五材無眚，刑罰不用，禮義興行，和氣氤氳，淳風澹泊。

translations.literal: Now the hundred grains have years, the five materials without calamity, punishments unused, ritual and righteousness arising, harmonious qi dense, pure wind tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: Grains have years, materials without calamity, punishments unused, ritual arising, qi harmonious, wind pure.

sentences.zh: 蠻夷戎狄，殊方異類，重譯而至者，日月于闕廷；

translations.literal: Barbarians, foreigners, and peoples of strange lands, through repeated translation arriving—daily at the court gate;
translations.idiomatic: Barbarians and strange peoples, translated, arrive daily at court;

sentences.zh: 奇獸神禽，甘露嘉醴，窮祥極瑞，朝夕于林禦。

translations.literal: strange beasts and divine birds, sweet dew and fine wine, omens and blessings to the limit—morning and evening in the imperial forest.
translations.idiomatic: strange beasts, sweet dew, omens to the limit—morning and evening in the forest.

sentences.zh: 王公卿士，罄乃誠於中；

translations.literal: Dukes, ministers, and gentlemen exhaust sincerity within;
translations.idiomatic: Dukes and gentlemen exhaust sincerity within;

sentences.zh: 鴻生碩儒，獻其書於外。

translations.literal: great scholars and erudites present their writings outside.
translations.idiomatic: great scholars present writings outside.

sentences.zh: 莫不以神祇合契，億兆同心。

translations.literal: All say spirits and sovereigns accord, billions of hearts unite.
translations.idiomatic: All say spirits accord, hearts unite.

sentences.zh: 斯皆烈祖聖孝，垂裕余慶。

translations.literal: These are all the fierce ancestors' sagely filiality, extending surplus blessing.
translations.idiomatic: These are fierce ancestors' filiality, extending blessing.

sentences.zh: 故朕賴宗廟之介福，敢以眇身，顓其克讓。

translations.literal: Therefore I rely on the ancestral temples' mediating fortune and dare with this slight person single out my yielding.
translations.idiomatic: I rely on temples' fortune and dare single out my yielding.

sentences.zh: 是以敬奉群議，弘此大猷，以光我高祖之丕圖，以紹我高祖之鴻烈。

translations.literal: Therefore I respectfully follow the group's proposals and expand this great plan, to glorify my High Ancestor's great design and continue my High Ancestor's great blaze.
translations.idiomatic: I follow proposals and expand this plan to glorify and continue the High Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 永言陟配，追感載深。

translations.literal: Forever speaking of ascending as match, recalling with deep gratitude beyond measure.
translations.idiomatic: Forever ascending as match—recalling with deep gratitude beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 可以開元十三年十一月十日，式遵故實，有事太山。

translations.literal: On the tenth day of the eleventh month of the thirteenth year of Kaiyuan, following former precedent, there will be affairs at Mount Tai.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyuan 13, month 11, day 10, following precedent, affairs at Mount Tai.

sentences.zh: 所司與公卿諸儒詳擇典禮，預為備具，勿廣勞人，務存節約，以稱朕意。

translations.literal: Let the relevant offices with dukes, ministers, and Confucians carefully select canonical rites, prepare in advance, do not broadly labor the people, preserve economy, to match my intent.
translations.idiomatic: Offices with dukes and Confucians: select rites, prepare, spare the people, preserve economy.

sentences.zh: 於是詔中書令張說、右散騎常侍徐堅、太常少卿韋絛、秘書少監康子元、國子博士侯行果等，與禮官於集賢書院刊撰儀注。
